correctness.rationale: The verifier reconstructs the 14-vertex, 21-edge Heawood graph from the Fano incidence rule; enumerates all 154 independent triples and all 15,900 faces; constructs 7,932 staged element-matching pairs; directly checks the entire 109,410-edge Hasse diagram for acyclicity; and leaves exactly 36 critical cells, all in dimension 8, with the empty face matched. Discrete Morse theory therefore gives one 0-cell plus 36 8-cells, hence the claimed wedge. Independent mod-2 chain ranks yield reduced Betti number 36 only in degree 8. No infinite assertion is inferred from sampling.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical highly symmetric incidence graph and a natural nonchordal bipartite test case for the total-cut construction. The defining literature gives exact families but does not determine this case. The exact wedge decomposition, not merely a numerical homology value, supplies a reusable benchmark for total-cut topology outside those families; the sphere multiplicity 36 and dimension 8 are not implied by the inspected theorems.
